clue.text: Unreadable code found in deniable engineering

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
engineering something means rebuilding or contriving it, so the word it follows is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a cipher is a secret code

explanation.surface: A secret code turns up hidden inside some plausibly deniable piece of engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineering' reads as a field of work, but it tells you to rebuild the word before it, which then splits around the code.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that cannot be deciphered is impossible to read, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: In time, bore whole number

parts.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time
eger is a variant spelling of eagre, a tidal bore or surge up a river

explanation.surface: Someone complains that, in time, a whole number became boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a verb or a dull person, but it is the tidal wave on a river, spelt here in its rarer form EGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a number with no fractional part, a whole number in arithmetic.

clue.text: Area of airport idle after change to customs?

indicators.note: after tells us the piece for idle is placed behind the other piece in the answer

parts.note: a departure is a change from usual custom or practice
to lounge is to laze about idly

explanation.surface: An airport zone sits idle once the customs procedures are changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests the airport's customs hall, but here it means habits: a departure from them is a change.
explanation.definitionFit: The departure lounge is the waiting area in an airport terminal where passengers sit before boarding.

clue.text: Corby emptied, accepting appeal leads to Birmingham perhaps

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the second piece goes inside the first
an emptied word has lost all its insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Corby
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A depopulated Corby, gaining appeal, might grow into somewhere like Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Corby is an English town in Northamptonshire. 'It' for sex appeal is a crossword convention from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birmingham is an example of a city, flagged by 'perhaps' as one instance of the class.

clue.text: Staff taken in by wages in satire

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: pay means wages
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees fooled by a pay deal end up in a satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it is a stick, which sits inside the word for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a mocking imitation, a form of satire.

clue.text: Bird recently died, behaved like a parrot

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
as in 'of late', meaning recently
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A pet bird that recently died used to copy everything like a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to copy someone, so behaving like a parrot is imitating, which is what emulated means.

clue.text: Biting a cord, hospital department follows

indicators.note: follows says the hospital department is placed after the earlier pieces

parts.note: taken as written
string is a thin cord
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone bites through a cord, and a hospital department deals with the aftermath.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are harsh and cutting, so biting is a synonym in the sense of sharp criticism.

clue.text: Immediate exit for Labour? It may shock some!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a walkout by workers called without warning
second meaning: a bolt from a thunderstorm can electrocute people

explanation.surface: A quick Labour departure from government would come as a jolt to some voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, but it is workers in general, who stage a sudden strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an unannounced industrial walkout and a strike of lightning that delivers an electric shock.

clue.text: Fixes jams

definitions.meaning: first meaning: attaches or glues in place
second meaning: gets stuck and will not move

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests repairing jams; the two words are separate meanings of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both fastening something with adhesive and becoming stuck, as a drawer does.

clue.text: Better adviser dumps half of rubbish in public

parts.note: tips are rubbish dumps

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one of its two halves, here the second

parts.note: the second half of litter, rubbish dropped in public places

explanation.surface: A wise counsellor drops half the rubbish in public places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is not a comparison but one who bets; the adviser gives racing tips.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives punters advice on which horse to back, so serves as an adviser to someone who bets.

clue.text: Tense putt played around international golf hard

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on either side of the following pieces
a putt that is played is made in a new way, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the abbreviation for international
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A nervous golfer plays a putt in a hard international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uptight is anxious and tense, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Start turning right, like when joining motorway

indicators.note: joining says the motorway letter is attached to the end
turning round makes these letters run the opposite way

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
e.g. means for example, like
M is the prefix for British motorways, as in M1

explanation.surface: A driving instruction: start by turning right, as you would when getting onto a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: R and EG run backwards to make GER, then the motorway letter joins on.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the beginning from which something grows, as in the germ of an idea.

clue.text: Independent trade commission essentially provoke laughter — 50 per cent off is impractical

indicators.note: taking fifty per cent off removes half of the word just before it

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
to deal is to trade

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, so only its middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of commission
to tickle is to make someone laugh

explanation.surface: An independent trade body's plan to stir up mirth at half price is unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickle loses its second half to leave TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic plans pursue perfection over what can actually be done, so they can be called impractical.

clue.text: Pen, beginning to drip upon odd instrument

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece upon another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: police kettle protesters by penning them in a confined area

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of drip
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A fountain pen drips its ink onto a strange musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool, but it is a verb for confining people, which is what kettling is.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum, or timpani, is a large orchestral percussion instrument.

clue.text: Recycles puzzles book left out

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: rebuses are picture puzzles
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone recycles a book of puzzles, leaving one out.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycling something means using it again, which is what reuses means.

clue.text: Sign up rashly to enclose space for birds

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap around the space
doing something rashly is done carelessly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an en is a printing space, half an em

explanation.surface: An impulsive volunteer signs up to fence off some space for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting unit of space, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguins are flightless seabirds of the southern hemisphere.

clue.text: Occasionally sick fellow involves a bit of nursing

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold or wrap around, so the pieces enclose the next ones

parts.note: off means unwell, as in feeling off
taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of here takes only a small part, the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of nursing
a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college

explanation.surface: An ill colleague brings in a spot of nursing care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick fellow' is read as one unit that wraps around the middle letters. A don is a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done off and on happens intermittently, now and then, so occasionally.

clue.text: Ornament rather frames Kipling poem

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: pretty means rather, as in pretty good
If— is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A decorative piece rather neatly frames a printed Kipling poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ornament' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament something is to decorate it, and to prettify is to make it look pretty.

clue.text: Puts down aims of Republicans, perhaps "make America over"

indicators.note: make X Y says one letter is made into another, swapping it in place

parts.note: the planks of a party platform are its declared policies
A is the abbreviation for America
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Republican goals evoke the slogan about making America great again.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in PLANKS becomes O. Plank is mainly a US political term for a single policy in a party platform.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk something is to put it down heavily and carelessly, a British informal verb.

clue.text: Mystery Magazine republished, dismissing literary ends

indicators.note: republished material is reissued in a new form, so letters are rearranged
dismissing means sending away, so some letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
the two ends of the alphabet of letters, A and Z

explanation.surface: A mystery magazine reissued without its literary closing sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary' is read as 'of letters': the ends of the alphabet are A and Z. Removing them leaves six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is something puzzling or inexplicable, a synonym of mystery.

clue.text: Gave end away, as the lead in Hamlet did?

definitions.text: as the lead in Hamlet did?

indicators.note: letters sent away are scattered and come back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spoiled the ending, telling what Hamlet's hero does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave end away' reads as giving a spoiler; the question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Hamlet kills Claudius to take revenge for his father's murder, so he avenged him.

clue.text: Peak of success when cycling, with belief to come first

indicators.note: to come first places the belief at the front of the answer
cycling moves letters round in a loop, so a front letter moves to the back

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhist belief
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A cyclist's peak of success comes when belief is put first.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling moves the first letter of HIT to the back to give ITH.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the highest point reached, the summit or peak of something.

clue.text: Belt actor losing head going after Oscar in atmospheric part

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off
going after places these pieces behind the letter for Oscar

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a belt is a zone or region, as in the commuter belt
a player is an actor

explanation.surface: An actor gets belted after losing his head over an Oscar ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer is a region of Earth's stratosphere, part of the atmosphere that absorbs ultraviolet light.

clue.text: Selection of best yeast for swelling

indicators.note: a selection takes a run of letters out of the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of best and the start of yeast

explanation.surface: Choosing the finest yeast for dough that is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swelling' suggests rising bread dough, but it is the noun for an inflamed lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid.

clue.text: Surround body of water to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going to the north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a pool is a small body of water

explanation.surface: An instruction to encircle a lake lying to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: To loop something is to encircle it with a curve, so surround fits as a verb.

clue.text: Benevolent socialist family

parts.note: kind means benevolent
red is a common term for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A description of a kind-hearted left-wing household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family' is a noun here; one's kindred are one's relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's relatives collectively, the people related by blood.

clue.text: Evening club in Guildford's opening

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Guildford

explanation.surface: An evening golf club meeting at a new Guildford venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' reads as night-time, but it is the verb even, smoothing out creases. Guildford is a town in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing flattens creases, so it is evening out cloth in the sense of making it smooth.

clue.text: Dog some Europeans in group

parts.note: Germans are one group of Europeans
hep is dated slang for fashionable, in
a herd is a group of animals

explanation.surface: A dog belonging to a group of Europeans travelling together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is an adjective meaning trendy, giving HEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The German shepherd is a breed of large working dog, also called the Alsatian.
